steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges and toss them with the cornflour, oil and salt. The cornflour helps them crisp.
Spread them out on a tray without crowding and roast for about 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp at the edges.
Stir the smoked paprika into the mayonnaise. Mix the yogurt with the chives, lemon juice and salt.
Serve the wedges hot with both dips on the side.
keep: Keep them covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat on a tray in a hot oven (220°C) for about 10 minutes so they crisp up again; the microwave makes them soft.

title: Gnocchi di ricotta in crema di zucchine, stracciatella e alici
summary: Light ricotta gnocchi in a courgette cream, topped with stracciatella and anchovies.
steps: Mix the drained ricotta with the egg yolk, Parmigiano and flour into a soft dough. Roll it into ropes on a floured board and cut into small gnocchi.
Cook the courgettes and shallot in the oil until soft, then blend them with a little water into a smooth cream. Season with salt.
Boil the gnocchi in salted water and lift them out as soon as they float.
Toss them gently in the warm courgette cream and serve topped with stracciatella and anchovies.
keep: Keep it in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat it in a pan with a splash of water to loosen the sauce, or let it come to room temperature if it's an oil-based dish.

title: Polpettine di manzo in salsa verde
summary: Small beef meatballs with a sharp green sauce of parsley, capers and anchovy.
steps: Mix the beef with the egg, Parmigiano, breadcrumbs and salt, and roll into small meatballs.
Brown them in a little oil in a pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Blend the parsley, capers, anchovies, vinegar and the rest of the oil into a bright green sauce.
Spoon the sauce over the warm meatballs and serve.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Filetti di orata con maionese alle acciughe e peperoncino
summary: Crisp-skinned sea bream fillets with a punchy anchovy and chili mayonnaise.
steps: Score the skin of the fish lightly and pat the fillets very dry, so the skin crisps.

Heat the oil in a frying pan until shimmering and lay the fillets in skin side down, pressing them gently for the first few seconds so they don't curl. Cook for about 4 minutes, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Mix the mayonnaise with the mashed anchovies, chili and lemon juice.
Serve the fish skin side up with a spoonful of the sauce.
keep: Seafood is best eaten the day it's cooked. If you have leftovers, cool them quickly, keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day, reheating gently.

title: Risotto alla crema di zucca Hokkaido e porri
summary: Risotto with a velvety Hokkaido pumpkin cream and gently sweated leeks.
steps: Cook the diced pumpkin in a little of the stock until soft, then blend it into a smooth cream.
Melt half the butter and sweat the sliced leek gently for 5 minutes, then add the rice, toast it for 2 minutes and pour in the wine.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, for about 15 minutes, then stir in the pumpkin cream and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more.
Take it off the heat and beat in the rest of the butter and the Parmigiano. Rest for a minute before serving.
keep: Cool risotto quickly, within an hour, then keep it covered in the fridge and eat it within 1 day. Reheat it in a pan with a splash of stock until piping hot, or roll it into balls, coat in breadcrumbs and fry as arancini.

title: Shio ramen
summary: A clear, golden chicken and kombu broth seasoned simply with salt. The lightest and oldest style of ramen.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chicken fat or neutral oil
steps: Put the chicken stock and kombu in a pot and warm it gently for about 20 minutes, keeping it just below a simmer. Lift out the kombu before it boils, or it turns slimy and bitter.
Make the tare by stirring the salt, light soy sauce and sake into a ladle of the hot broth. Divide it between two deep bowls along with the chicken fat or oil.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, usually 1 to 2 minutes, and drain them really well: water left on the noodles dilutes the broth.
Pour the hot broth into the bowls and stir to mix with the tare, then add the noodles and lift them with chopsticks so they sit neatly.
Top with the chashu or chicken, the halved egg, spring onion and a sheet of nori tucked at the side. Eat straight away, while the noodles are springy.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Shoyu ramen
summary: Tokyo-style ramen in a clear chicken and dashi broth seasoned with a savoury soy tare.
steps: Heat the chicken stock and dashi together in a pot until steaming.
For the tare, simmer the soy sauce, mirin and sake in a small pan for 1 minute to cook off the alcohol. Divide it and the oil between two deep bowls.
Cook the noodles as the packet says and drain them well.
Pour the hot broth into the bowls and stir, then add the noodles.
Arrange the chashu, marinated egg, menma, spring onion and nori on top and serve straight away.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Miso ramen
summary: Sapporo's rich, nutty miso ramen with stir-fried pork and vegetables, sweet corn and a pat of butter.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok or wide pot over high heat and stir-fry the pork with the garlic and ginger until browned. Add the bean sprouts and cabbage and toss for 2 minutes, until just wilted.
Pour in the stock and bring it to a simmer.
In a bowl, whisk the miso and sesame paste with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. From here on, keep it below the boil so the miso stays fragrant.
Cook the noodles, drain well and divide between deep bowls. Ladle over the broth and vegetables.
Top with the sweetcorn, a pat of butter that melts into the broth, and spring onion.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Tonkotsu ramen
summary: Hakata's creamy pork bone broth, boiled hard for hours until it turns milky white. A weekend project.
ingredients: 2 kg pork trotters and neck bones
Pickled ginger and sesame, to serve
steps: Put the bones in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil for 10 minutes. Drain, then rinse the bones and scrub off the grey scum. This keeps the finished broth clean.

Return the bones to the clean pot with fresh water, the onion, garlic and ginger. Keep it at a hard, rolling boil for 10 to 12 hours, topping up with boiling water as it reduces. The vigorous boil breaks down the collagen and turns the broth milky white.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and season it with the soy sauce and salt.
Cook the thin noodles for about 1 minute so they stay firm, drain and add them to bowls of the hot broth.
Top with chashu, the halved eggs, spring onion, pickled ginger and sesame.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Black garlic ramen
summary: Creamy pork broth swirled with mayu, a bittersweet black garlic oil made by slowly burning garlic in sesame oil. Start with tonkotsu broth made ahead.
ingredients: 1 l tonkotsu or rich pork broth
steps: Put the chopped garlic and neutral oil in a small pan over medium-low heat and cook, stirring all the time, for about 15 minutes. The garlic will go golden, then brown, then completely black. Open a window: it smokes a little.
Take it off the heat, let it cool for a few minutes, then add the sesame oil and blend until smooth and inky. This black garlic oil is mayu, bittersweet and smoky.
Heat the pork broth with the soy sauce.
Cook the noodles, drain well and add them to bowls of hot broth.
Drizzle a spoonful or two of mayu over each bowl and top with chashu, the halved egg, wood ear mushrooms and spring onion.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Miso butter corn ramen
summary: A vegetarian take on Hokkaido miso ramen with a kombu and shiitake broth, sweet corn, butter and a soft egg.
steps: Put the kombu and dried shiitake in the water and leave them to soak for 30 minutes. Then warm the pot slowly and lift out the kombu just before it boils.
Simmer the broth with the shiitake for 10 minutes, then take them out, slice them and return them to the pot.
Turn the heat down so the broth is no longer bubbling, and whisk in the miso, soy sauce and ginger.
Cook the noodles, drain them well and divide between bowls. Pour over the hot broth.
Top with the corn, a pat of butter, the halved egg, bean sprouts and spring onion.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Vegan shoyu ramen with crispy tofu
summary: A deep, savoury shiitake and kombu shoyu broth with crispy tofu, bok choy and egg-free noodles.
steps: Soak the kombu and dried shiitake in the water for 30 minutes, then simmer gently for 15 minutes and strain. Slice the softened shiitake and keep them for the top.
Season the broth with the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil, and keep it hot.
Toss the tofu cubes in cornflour and fry them in the oil over medium-high heat, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides. Blanch the bok choy for 1 minute.
Cook the egg-free noodles, drain well and add them to bowls of the hot broth.
Top with the crispy tofu, bok choy, shiitake, spring onion and a sheet of nori.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Vegan tantanmen
summary: A creamy sesame and soy milk broth with chili oil and savoury soy mince. Rich, spicy and fully plant-based.
ingredients: 3 tbsp tahini or Chinese sesame paste
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the rehydrated soy mince with the garlic and ginger, stirring, until browned and a little crisp. Season with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce.
In each serving bowl, whisk the tahini, miso and the remaining soy sauce into a smooth paste.
Warm the soy milk and stock together gently, without letting them boil, or the soy milk can split. Pour into the bowls a little at a time, whisking, so the broth turns creamy.
Cook the noodles and blanch the bok choy, then add both to the bowls.
Top with the soy mince and spring onion and finish with a generous drizzle of chili oil.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Tantanmen
summary: Japan's version of Sichuan dan dan noodles: spicy minced pork over noodles in a sesame-rich broth.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the minced pork with the garlic, ginger and doubanjiang, breaking it up, until browned and crisp at the edges.
In each serving bowl, mix the sesame paste, soy sauce and vinegar into a smooth paste.
Pour in the hot stock a little at a time, stirring, until the broth is creamy.
Cook the noodles and blanch the bok choy, then add them to the bowls.
Top with the spicy pork and spring onion and finish with chili oil.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Tsukemen
summary: Dipping ramen: thick, chilled noodles served beside a hot, concentrated pork and fish dipping broth.
ingredients: 500 ml rich pork or chicken stock
steps: Put the stock, soy sauce, mirin, vinegar, sugar and katsuobushi in a pan and simmer for 10 minutes, then strain. The dipping broth should taste much stronger than a normal ramen soup, with a gentle sourness, because it only coats the noodles.
Cook the thick noodles as the packet says, then rinse them under cold running water and drain well. Chilling them firms them up and gives them their springy bite.
Pile the noodles on plates with the chashu, halved egg and nori.
Pour the hot broth into small bowls and add the spring onion. Dip a mouthful of noodles into the broth as you eat.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Hiyashi chuka
summary: Cold ramen salad for hot days: chilled noodles under colourful strips of ham, cucumber, egg and tomato, with a tangy soy dressing.
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil with 2 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves, then chill the dressing.
Beat the eggs and cook them in a lightly oiled pan as two or three thin omelettes. Roll them up and slice into fine ribbons.
Cook the noodles, then rinse them in iced water until completely cold and drain very well.
Pile the noodles on plates and arrange the egg, cucumber, ham and tomato on top in neat colourful rows.
Pour over the dressing and finish with sesame seeds and a dab of mustard on the side.
keep: Best eaten freshly made. Keep the toppings and the sauce or dressing in separate containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you want to eat it.

title: Mazesoba
summary: Brothless ramen from Nagoya: thick noodles tossed at the table with spicy minced pork, garlic chives, nori and a raw egg yolk.
steps: Fry the minced pork with the garlic and doubanjiang in a hot pan until browned and crisp, then stir in 1 tbsp of the soy sauce.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, the sesame oil and the chili oil in the bottom of each bowl.
Cook the thick noodles, drain them well and toss them in the sauce while they're hot.
Top with the spicy pork, chives, shredded nori, katsuobushi and an egg yolk in the middle.
Mix everything together vigorously at the table, so the yolk turns into a glossy sauce that coats the noodles.
keep: Best eaten freshly made. Keep the toppings and the sauce or dressing in separate containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you want to eat it.

title: Tacos al pastor
summary: Pork marinated in chilies, achiote and pineapple, seared until charred and piled into corn tortillas. Marinate for 2 hours first.
steps: Toast the dried chilies in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side, until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes. Drain and blend with the achiote, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano and a good pinch of salt into a smooth paste.
Coat the sliced pork in the marinade and leave it for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat a heavy pan or griddle until very hot and sear the pork in batches, without crowding, until it's charred at the edges. Chop it into small pieces.
Sear the diced pineapple in the same pan until caramelised. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Fill each tortilla with pork, pineapple, chopped onion and coriander, and finish with a squeeze of lime.
keep: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, separate from the bread or tortillas and the fresh toppings. Reheat the filling in a hot pan and warm the bread just before serving.

title: Guacamole con totopos
summary: Chunky avocado mashed with lime, chili, onion and coriander, served with crisp tortilla chips.
steps: Put the chopped onion, chili and a pinch of salt in a bowl, or a molcajete if you have one, and mash them into a rough paste. This releases their flavour into the avocado.
Halve the avocados, scoop out the flesh and mash it into the paste with a fork, leaving it chunky.
Fold in the tomato, coriander and lime juice.
Taste and add more salt or lime, then serve straight away with tortilla chips, before the avocado starts to brown.
keep: Guacamole browns quickly. Press cling film right onto the surface and keep it in the fridge for up to 1 day, then give it a stir before serving.

title: Pozole rojo
summary: A deep red pork and hominy soup, served with crunchy toppings so everyone builds their own bowl.
ingredients: Shredded cabbage, sliced radish, lime and tostadas, to serve
steps: Put the pork in a large pot with half the onion, 2 garlic cloves, salt and 3 l water. Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer gently for 1½ hours, until the meat is tender.

Toast the chilies in a dry pan for a few seconds per side, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes. Blend with the rest of the onion and garlic and a cup of the broth, and strain the sauce into the pot.
Add the hominy and oregano and simmer for 30 minutes more, so the broth turns deep red and the flavours come together. Season with salt.
Serve in deep bowls with the shredded cabbage, sliced radish, lime wedges and tostadas on the side, so everyone can add their own crunch.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Enchiladas verdes
summary: Corn tortillas rolled around shredded chicken and baked under a tangy tomatillo salsa with cream and cheese.
ingredients: 120 g queso fresco or feta, crumbled
steps: Put the tomatillos, chilies, onion and garlic in a pan, cover with water and simmer for about 8 minutes, until the tomatillos turn olive green. Drain and blend with the coriander and salt.
Heat the oil in a pan and pour in the salsa carefully, as it will splutter. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens slightly and thickens.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Warm the tortillas so they're soft and pliable, fill each with chicken and roll it up. Lay them seam side down in a baking dish.
Pour the salsa over the enchiladas, spoon over the crème fraîche and scatter with cheese.
Bake for about 15 minutes, until hot and bubbling at the edges.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Cochinita pibil
summary: Yucatán's slow-roasted pork in achiote and citrus, wrapped in banana leaves and served with pink pickled onions.
steps: Blend the achiote paste with the orange and lime juice, garlic, cumin and a good pinch of salt. Rub it all over the pork and leave to marinate, overnight in the fridge if you can.
Line a roasting dish with banana leaves, lay the pork on top with the marinade and fold the leaves over. Cover tightly with foil and roast at 160°C for about 3½ hours, until the meat falls apart.
Meanwhile, put the sliced onions and habanero in a jar. Heat the vinegar with a pinch of salt and pour it over. After an hour the onions turn bright pink.
Shred the pork with two forks and mix it with its juices. Serve in warm tortillas topped with the pickled onions.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Chilaquiles rojos
summary: Crisp tortilla chips simmered briefly in red salsa and topped with a fried egg, cream and cheese. Mexico's favourite breakfast.
ingredients: Sliced onion and coriander, to serve
steps: Soak the dried chili in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend it with the tomatoes, garlic and onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide pan, pour in the salsa and simmer for about 8 minutes, until it thickens and darkens. Season with salt.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs in a separate pan until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Add the tortilla chips to the hot salsa and toss for about a minute. They should soften at the edges but keep some crunch.
Plate straight away and top with the eggs, crème fraîche, crumbled cheese, sliced onion and coriander.
keep: Best eaten fresh, because the eggs and crisp bits don't reheat well. Leftover sauce keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Warm it up and cook fresh eggs in it.

title: Churros con chocolate
summary: Crisp ridged dough sticks rolled in cinnamon sugar, for dipping into thick hot chocolate.
steps: Put the water, butter, sugar and a pinch of salt in a pan and bring to the boil. Tip in the flour all at once and beat hard with a wooden spoon until the dough comes away from the sides in a smooth ball.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until the dough is glossy and smooth.

Heat the oil to 180°C. Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star nozzle and pipe 10 cm lengths straight into the oil, snipping them off with scissors. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain briefly and roll the hot churros in the cinnamon sugar.
For the chocolate, whisk the milk with the cornflour, add the chocolate and heat gently, whisking, until thick and glossy. Serve in cups for dipping.
keep: These are best eaten fresh, while they're crisp. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day. Reheat them on a tray in a hot oven (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes to crisp them up again, rather than in the microwave.

title: Birria ramen
summary: Slow-braised birria beef in a chili and spice broth, served over ramen noodles with onion, coriander and lime.
ingredients: Chopped onion, coriander and lime, to serve
steps: Toast the dried chilies in a dry pan for a few seconds per side, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes. Blend with the onion, garlic, tomatoes, spices and vinegar until smooth.
Brown the beef well in a heavy pot. Pour over the chili sauce and 1.5 l water, bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for about 3 hours, until the meat falls apart.
Lift out the beef and shred it. Skim some of the red fat from the top of the broth and keep it for drizzling. Season the broth with salt.
Cook the noodles, drain them and add them to bowls of the hot broth with the shredded beef.
Drizzle with the red fat and finish with chopped onion, coriander and a squeeze of lime.
keep: Keep the broth and the toppings in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and cook fresh noodles when you reheat: noodles left sitting in broth turn soft. Bring the broth back to a simmer before serving.

title: Cauliflower tacos with chipotle crema
summary: Spiced roasted cauliflower in warm tortillas with a smoky cashew and chipotle crema and quick pickled cabbage.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the cauliflower florets with the oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt, spread them out on a tray and roast for about 25 minutes, until tender and charred at the edges.
Drain the soaked cashews and blend them with the chipotle, half the lime juice, salt and a splash of water until very smooth and pourable.
Toss the shredded cabbage with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and let it sit while the cauliflower roasts.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with cauliflower, pickled cabbage, a drizzle of chipotle crema and coriander. Squeeze over the rest of the lime.
keep: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, separate from the bread or tortillas and the fresh toppings. Reheat the filling in a hot pan and warm the bread just before serving.

title: Esquites bowl with feta and lime
summary: Street-cart esquites turned into a fresh salad bowl: charred corn, lime, chili, herbs, avocado and crumbled feta.
steps: Heat a large, dry frying pan until very hot, add the corn and leave it to char for a minute before stirring. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes in total, until blistered and golden in places, then stir in the butter.
Mix the mayonnaise with the lime juice, chili powder and a pinch of salt.
Toss the warm corn with the dressing, chopped onion and coriander.
Spoon into bowls, top with the avocado and crumbled feta, and dust with a little more chili.
keep: Salads are best fresh. To keep some, store the undressed ingredients in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress them just before eating. Keep crunchy things like toasted bread or nuts separate until the last minute.

title: Butter chicken
summary: Tandoori-style chicken in a silky tomato, butter and cream sauce scented with fenugreek. Delhi's most famous export.
steps: Mix the yogurt with half the garam masala, the chili powder, garlic, ginger and salt, and coat the chicken. Leave it to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the chicken under a hot grill or in a very hot pan until it's charred in places and just cooked through. The charring gives the dish its smoky, tandoori flavour.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the passata and the rest of the garam masala and simmer for about 10 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Stir in the cream and sugar, then crumble in the dried fenugreek leaves between your fingers.
Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes so it absorbs the sauce. Serve with rice or naan.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Dal tadka
summary: Yellow lentils cooked soft and finished with a sizzling tempering of ghee, cumin, garlic and chili.
ingredients: 250 g yellow lentils (toor or moong dal)
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put them in a pot with the turmeric, tomato and 1 l water, bring to the boil, skim, and simmer for about 25 minutes, until completely soft. Season with salt and whisk to a creamy consistency.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan until shimmering. Add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for a few seconds.
Add the garlic, dried chilies and asafoetida and cook until the garlic turns golden. Watch it closely: it goes from golden to burnt very quickly.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal. It will hiss and fill the kitchen with its aroma. Finish with coriander and serve with rice.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Chana masala
summary: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy, spiced onion and tomato gravy. Hearty, cheap and naturally vegan.
ingredients: 2 tsp chana masala or garam masala
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pan and add the cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add the onions and cook over medium heat for about 12 minutes, stirring, until deep golden. Taking your time here gives the curry its rich flavour.
Add the garlic, ginger and chili and cook for a minute, then add the tomatoes and the spice mix. Cook, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil starts to separate from the sauce.
Add the chickpeas and a cup of water and simmer for about 15 minutes. Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the amchur for a gentle sourness, season with salt and finish with coriander.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Palak paneer
summary: Cubes of soft paneer in a smooth, garlicky spinach sauce.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then plunge it into iced water so it stays bright green. Squeeze it out and blend until smooth.
Fry the paneer cubes in a little of the ghee until golden on a couple of sides, then set them aside.
Heat the rest of the ghee, add the cumin seeds, then the onion, garlic, ginger and chili, and cook until soft and golden.
Add the spinach purée and garam masala, season with salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and the paneer and warm through gently before serving.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Hyderabadi chicken biryani
summary: Layers of spiced chicken and saffron basmati rice, sealed and slow-steamed so the flavours meet.
ingredients: 2 onions, thinly sliced and fried crisp
1 pinch saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves and 1 bay leaf
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, biryani masala, chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, half the fried onions and salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then boil it in plenty of salted water with the whole spices until about 70% cooked: the grains should still be firm in the centre. Drain.

Spread the marinated chicken in an even layer in a heavy pot. Cover it with the rice, then scatter over the mint, coriander and remaining fried onions, drizzle with the saffron milk and dot with ghee.
Seal the pot tightly with foil and a lid and cook on the lowest heat for about 40 minutes. The chicken cooks in its own juices and steams the rice from below.
Rest for 10 minutes before opening, then mix gently from the bottom as you serve, so everyone gets chicken and rice.
keep: Cool rice dishes quickly, within an hour, then keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day. Reheat until piping hot all the way through, adding a splash of water so the rice doesn't dry out.

title: Aloo gobi
summary: Potatoes and cauliflower stir-fried with turmeric, cumin and ginger until tender and golden.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the ginger, chili, turmeric and ground coriander and cook for a minute.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower with salt and a splash of water, stir to coat them in the spices, cover and cook on low heat for about 20 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender.
Take off the lid and turn up the heat for a few minutes so the edges crisp and colour. Finish with garam masala and coriander.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Kerala fish curry (meen moilee)
summary: White fish poached in a mild, fragrant coconut sauce with curry leaves, ginger and turmeric.
ingredients: 600 g firm white fish, in pieces
steps: Rub the fish pieces with the turmeric and a pinch of salt and set them aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seeds. When they start to pop, add the curry leaves, onion, ginger and chilies, and cook gently until the onion is soft.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring it to a gentle simmer. Don't let it boil hard, or it may split.
Slide in the fish and tomato slices and poach gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fish flakes easily. Season and finish with a squeeze of lime.
keep: Seafood is best eaten the day it's cooked. If you have leftovers, cool them quickly, keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day, reheating gently.

title: Paneer tikka tacos with mint chutney
summary: A street-food mash-up: charred paneer tikka in soft tortillas or mini naan with mint chutney and pickled onions.
steps: Mix 100 g of the yogurt with the tikka masala, chili powder and salt, and coat the paneer cubes and pepper chunks. Leave for 20 minutes.
Toss the sliced onion with the lime juice and a pinch of salt and let it soften while the paneer marinates.
Blend the mint, coriander, chili, the remaining yogurt and salt into a smooth green chutney.
Grill or pan-fry the paneer and pepper over high heat until charred at the edges. Warm the tortillas or naan, then fill them and top with the pickled onion and chutney.
keep: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, separate from the bread or tortillas and the fresh toppings. Reheat the filling in a hot pan and warm the bread just before serving.

title: Masala mac and cheese
summary: Comfort food with a kick: macaroni in a cheddar sauce spiced with turmeric and green chili, finished with a buttery cumin tempering.
steps: Cook the macaroni in salted water until just al dente, then drain.
Melt the butter in a pan, stir in the flour and cook for a minute. Whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth, then simmer for a few minutes until thick.
Stir in the turmeric, garam masala, chili and cheese until melted and glossy, then fold in the pasta.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds, then pour the tempering over the mac and cheese. Finish with coriander.
keep: Keep it in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat it in a pan with a splash of water to loosen the sauce, or let it come to room temperature if it's an oil-based dish.

title: Mango lassi panna cotta
summary: The flavours of a mango lassi set into a wobbly dessert with cardamom and pistachio, made with agar so it's vegetarian. Needs 2 hours to set.
steps: Put the cold cream, sugar and cardamom in a pan and whisk in the agar agar powder before you turn on the heat, so it doesn't clump.
Bring it to the boil, stirring, and let it bubble gently for 1 minute: agar only sets once it has boiled.
Take it off the heat and quickly whisk in the mango purée and yogurt. Work fast, as agar starts to set as it cools.
Pour into glasses and chill for at least 2 hours, until set. Top with chopped pistachios before serving.
keep: Keep it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Dairy-rich and set desserts shouldn't sit at room temperature for long.

title: Arayes
summary: Pita pockets filled with a thin layer of spiced minced meat, then grilled until the bread is crisp and the filling juicy. A Palestinian street-food favourite.
ingredients: 500 g minced lamb or beef, or a mix
Tahini sauce or yogurt, to serve
steps: Grate the onion and squeeze out as much juice as you can with your hands. Mix it with the meat, parsley, spices and salt, kneading until sticky.
Cut each pita in half to make two pockets. Open them carefully and spread a thin, even layer of meat inside, right to the edges, so it cooks through at the same time as the bread crisps.
Brush the outside of the pitas with olive oil.
Cook in a hot griddle pan, or in the oven at 220°C, for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until the bread is crisp and golden and the meat is cooked through.
Cut into wedges and serve hot with tahini sauce or yogurt.
keep: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, separate from the bread or tortillas and the fresh toppings. Reheat the filling in a hot pan and warm the bread just before serving.

title: Maqluba
summary: An upside-down pot of spiced rice, chicken and fried vegetables, flipped onto a tray at the table. The name means upside down.
ingredients: 400 g long-grain rice, soaked for 30 minutes
40 g toasted almonds or pine nuts
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the onion, cinnamon, cardamom, salt and 1.5 l water. Simmer for about 40 minutes, then lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Meanwhile, fry the aubergine slices, cauliflower and potato in hot oil, in batches, until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Drain the soaked rice and mix it with the seven spice and turmeric. In a deep, heavy pot, make a layer of chicken, then the fried vegetables, then the rice, pressing it down lightly.
Pour hot broth over the top until it covers the rice by about 2 cm. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on very low heat for 30 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes with the lid on.
Put a large tray on top of the pot and flip it over in one confident move. Tap the pot, lift it away and you have a golden dome. Scatter with toasted nuts and serve with yogurt.
keep: Cool rice dishes quickly, within an hour, then keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day. Reheat until piping hot all the way through, adding a splash of water so the rice doesn't dry out.

title: Musakhan
summary: Palestine's national dish: roast chicken on olive-oil-soaked flatbread, piled with sweet onions and tart, crimson sumac.
steps: Rub the chicken with half the sumac, the seven spice, cumin, salt and a little oil. Roast at 200°C for about 45 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the sliced onions very slowly in the rest of the olive oil with the remaining sumac and a pinch of salt, for about 25 minutes, until soft, sweet and stained purple.
Lay the flatbreads on a tray and brush them generously with the oniony oil from the pan, then spread the onions on top.
Place the chicken on the onions and warm in the oven for 5 minutes, so the bread crisps at the edges.
Scatter with toasted pine nuts and a final dusting of sumac and serve while warm.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: Hummus
summary: Silky chickpea and tahini dip. The trick is warm chickpeas and a splash of ice water for the fluffiest texture.
ingredients: Olive oil, paprika and parsley, to serve
steps: If you're using tinned chickpeas, warm them in their liquid for a few minutes, then drain. Warm chickpeas blend much smoother.
Blend the chickpeas with the garlic and lemon juice until they form a crumbly paste.

Add the tahini and cumin and blend again, then add the ice-cold water a spoonful at a time, with the blender running, until the hummus turns pale, smooth and fluffy. This can take a few minutes. Season with salt.
Spread it in a shallow bowl, making a swirl with the back of a spoon, and fill the dip with olive oil. Finish with paprika, a few whole chickpeas and chopped parsley.
keep: Keep it in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days, with a thin layer of olive oil on top to stop it drying out. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Falafel
summary: Crisp, herby fritters made from soaked raw chickpeas. Start soaking the night before.
ingredients: Pita, tahini sauce and salad, to serve
steps: Drain the soaked chickpeas and dry them well. They must be soaked but raw: cooked or tinned chickpeas make falafel that falls apart.
Put them in a food processor with the onion, garlic, herbs, spices and salt and pulse until finely chopped, like coarse sand that holds together when pressed. Stir in the baking soda.
Shape the mixture into small patties or balls with wet hands, pressing firmly.
Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the falafel in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until deep brown and crisp outside and green and fluffy inside.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve in warm pita with tahini sauce and salad.
keep: These are best eaten fresh, while they're crisp. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day. Reheat them on a tray in a hot oven (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes to crisp them up again, rather than in the microwave.

title: Fattoush
summary: A crunchy chopped salad with toasted pitta, herbs, sumac and a tangy pomegranate molasses dressing.
steps: Tear the pitta into bite-sized pieces, toss with 3 tbsp of the oil and spread on a tray. Bake at 200°C for about 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Chop the cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, radishes and spring onions into bite-sized pieces, and roughly tear the mint and parsley.
Whisk the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, sumac, the remaining oil and a pinch of salt into a tangy dressing.
Just before serving, toss the vegetables and herbs with the dressing, then fold in the crispy pitta so it stays crunchy.
keep: Salads are best fresh. To keep some, store the undressed ingredients in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress them just before eating. Keep crunchy things like toasted bread or nuts separate until the last minute.

title: Baba ghanoush
summary: Smoky charred aubergine mashed with tahini, lemon and garlic.
ingredients: Pomegranate seeds and parsley, to serve
steps: Prick the aubergines a few times and char them directly over a gas flame, on a barbecue or under a very hot grill, turning, for about 20 minutes, until the skin is blackened and the flesh completely soft. The charring gives the dip its smoky flavour.
Let them cool slightly, then split them open and scoop the flesh into a sieve. Leave it to drain for 10 minutes so the dip isn't watery.
Mash the flesh with a fork and stir in the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
Spread it in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and scatter with pomegranate seeds and parsley.
keep: Keep it in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days, with a thin layer of olive oil on top to stop it drying out. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Mujaddara
summary: Lentils and rice cooked together and crowned with a tangle of deeply browned, crispy onions. Humble and addictive.
steps: Rinse the lentils and boil them in plenty of water for about 15 minutes, until almost tender but still holding their shape. Drain.

Meanwhile, cook the sliced onions in the olive oil over medium heat, stirring often, for 20 to 25 minutes, until deep brown and crisp. Be patient: the dark, sweet onions are the heart of the dish. Lift out half and drain them on kitchen paper.

Add the rinsed rice, cumin, salt and lentils to the remaining onions and oil, stir, and pour in 500 ml water. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low heat for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and pile onto a platter. Top with the crispy onions and serve with salad or yogurt.
keep: Cool rice dishes quickly, within an hour, then keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day. Reheat until piping hot all the way through, adding a splash of water so the rice doesn't dry out.

title: Chicken shawarma
summary: Spiced, yogurt-marinated chicken roasted until charred, sliced thin and wrapped in flatbread with garlic sauce and pickles. Marinate for an hour first.
ingredients: Garlic sauce, pickles, tomato and parsley, to serve
steps: Mix the yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon and salt, and coat the chicken thighs well. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Spread the chicken on a tray and roast for about 25 minutes, then put it under a hot grill for a few minutes, until charred at the edges.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice it thinly.
Warm the flatbreads and fill them with the chicken, garlic sauce, pickles, tomato and parsley. Roll them up tightly and serve.
keep: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, separate from the bread or tortillas and the fresh toppings. Reheat the filling in a hot pan and warm the bread just before serving.

title: Knafeh
summary: Nablus's famous dessert: crisp shredded pastry over a layer of melting sweet cheese, soaked in orange blossom syrup. Best eaten warm.
ingredients: 300 g akkawi or mozzarella, soaked to remove the salt
steps: Make the syrup first: simmer the sugar, water and lemon juice for about 8 minutes, until slightly thickened. Stir in the orange blossom water and let it cool completely.
Pull the kataifi apart and chop it into short strands. Mix it with the melted butter until every strand is coated, and press half of it very firmly into a 26 cm pan.
Drain and pat dry the soaked cheese, mix it with the ricotta and spread it over the pastry, leaving a small border. Cover with the rest of the kataifi and press down.
Bake at 190°C for about 35 minutes, until deep golden. Turn it out onto a plate, pour over the cool syrup and scatter with pistachios. Serve warm, while the cheese is stretchy.
keep: Keep it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Dairy-rich desserts shouldn't sit at room temperature for long, and some contain raw egg.

title: Tabbouleh
summary: A bright parsley salad with a little bulgur, tomato, mint and plenty of lemon. More herbs than grain.
steps: Rinse the bulgur and put it in a bowl with the juice of 1 lemon and 2 tbsp water. Leave it for about 15 minutes to soften.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the parsley and mint well, then chop them very finely with a sharp knife. A blunt knife or food processor bruises the herbs and makes them soggy.
Mix the herbs with the tomatoes, spring onions and bulgur.
Dress with the olive oil, the remaining lemon juice, allspice and salt, and serve straight away. It should be mostly green, with just a little bulgur.
keep: Salads are best fresh. To keep some, store the undressed ingredients in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress them just before eating. Keep crunchy things like toasted bread or nuts separate until the last minute.

title: Freekeh soup
summary: A comforting Palestinian soup of smoky green wheat and chicken, often served during Ramadan.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the chicken and seven spice and cook until the chicken is lightly browned.
Add the rinsed freekeh and the stock, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 35 minutes, until the grains are tender and the soup has thickened.
Season with salt and stir in lemon juice to taste.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with chopped parsley.
keep: This keeps well: cool it, then store it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavour often gets even better overnight. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

title: High-protein chicken bowl
summary: Juicy spiced chicken breast over brown rice with edamame, broccoli and a creamy Greek yogurt and lemon sauce. Around 45 g of protein per bowl.
steps: Get the rice going first: rinse it, then simmer it in plenty of salted water for about 25 minutes until tender, and drain it well.
While it cooks, flatten the chicken breasts a little with your palm so they cook evenly, then rub them with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and a good pinch of salt.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until golden outside and no longer pink in the middle. Let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing, so the juices stay inside.
For the last 4 minutes of the rice, drop the broccoli and edamame into the same pot so everything is ready together.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, herbs and a pinch of salt to make the sauce.
Divide the rice, greens and cucumber between two bowls, lay the sliced chicken on top and spoon over the yogurt sauce.
keep: Cool rice dishes quickly, within an hour, then keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day. Reheat until piping hot all the way through, adding a splash of water so the rice doesn't dry out.

title: Healthy Mediterranean salad
summary: A big, crunchy salad of tomatoes, cucumber, peppers, chickpeas, olives and feta in a lemon and oregano dressing. Filling enough to eat as a meal.
steps: Put the sliced red onion in a small bowl with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and leave it for 5 minutes. This takes away the harsh bite.
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes, cucumber and pepper into bite-sized pieces and put them in a large bowl with the lettuce, chickpeas and olives.
Whisk the oil and oregano into the onion and lemon juice to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad, add the parsley and toss everything together well.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve straight away.
keep: Salads are best fresh. To keep some, store the undressed ingredients in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress them just before eating. Keep crunchy things like toasted bread or nuts separate until the last minute.

title: Garlic salmon rice bowl
summary: Salmon glazed in garlic, honey and soy, served over fluffy rice with avocado, cucumber and spinach. Quick, balanced and full of omega-3.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then cook it with 1½ times its volume of water, covered, on low heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes more.
Mix the garlic, soy sauce, honey and vinegar in a small bowl.
Pat the salmon dry and season it lightly. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and cook the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp, then turn it over.
Pour in the garlic sauce and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning it over the fish, until it turns sticky and the salmon is just cooked in the middle.
Fill the bowls with rice, spinach, avocado and cucumber, add the salmon and pour over any glaze left in the pan.
Finish with sesame seeds and spring onions.
keep: Seafood is best eaten the day it's cooked. If you have leftovers, cool them quickly, keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day, reheating gently.

title: Easy quinoa and vegetable bowl
summary: Fluffy quinoa with roasted sweet potato, peppers and courgette, chickpeas and a creamy lemon tahini dressing. Plant-based and great for meal prep.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the sweet potato, pepper, courgette and chickpeas with the oil, cumin and salt, spread them out on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden at the edges.

Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa well in a sieve, which removes its bitter coating. Simmer it in 240 ml salted water, covered, for 15 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff it with a fork.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and maple syrup, then add the warm water a little at a time until the dressing is smooth and pourable. Season with salt.
Divide the quinoa between two bowls with the spinach, pile the roasted vegetables on top and drizzle with the tahini dressing.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Healthy chicken wrap
summary: Lightly spiced grilled chicken rolled in wholemeal wraps with crisp salad and a garlic yogurt sauce. Lunch you can eat with one hand.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts in half through the middle so you have thin pieces that cook fast. Rub them with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt.
Cook them in a hot griddle or frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until browned and cooked through, then rest for a few minutes and slice into strips.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the wraps in a dry pan for a few seconds each side so they're soft and don't crack.
Spread each wrap with sauce, add lettuce, tomato, cucumber, onion and chicken in a line down the middle, then fold in the bottom and roll it up tightly. Cut in half to serve.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Greek chicken meal prep
summary: Lemon, garlic and oregano chicken with rice, a crunchy Greek salad and tzatziki, packed into four lunch boxes for the week ahead.
steps: Mix the oil, half the lemon juice, the garlic, oregano and salt in a bowl, add the chicken and leave it for at least 15 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Cook the rice: simmer it in 400 ml salted water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest it off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Spread the chicken out on a lined tray and roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Grate half the cucumber, squeeze out the water with your hands and stir it into the yogurt with the dill, the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. That's your tzatziki.
Dice the rest of the cucumber and toss it with the tomatoes, onion, olives and crumbled feta.
Let everything cool, then divide it between four containers, keeping the tzatziki in a small pot on the side so nothing goes soggy.
keep: Cool rice dishes quickly, within an hour, then keep them covered in the fridge and eat them within 1 day. Reheat until piping hot all the way through, adding a splash of water so the rice doesn't dry out.

title: Fluffy American pancakes
summary: Thick, soft pancakes that rise tall in the pan, served with butter, maple syrup and berries. The secret is a lumpy batter and a short rest.
ingredients: 30 g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
Maple syrup and berries, to serve
steps: Stir the lemon juice into the milk and leave it for 5 minutes. It will thicken slightly, like buttermilk, which makes the pancakes lighter.
In a big bowl, mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt.

Whisk the egg and melted butter into the milk, then pour it into the dry ingredients and stir gently with a fork until just combined. Stop while there are still small lumps: overmixing makes pancakes flat and tough.
Leave the batter to rest for 5 to 10 minutes while the pan heats up over medium-low heat.
Wipe the pan with a little butter, pour in about 3 tbsp of batter per pancake and cook until bubbles appear on top and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Keep them warm in a low oven while you cook the rest, then stack them up with butter, maple syrup and berries.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Easy overnight oats
summary: Oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt with chia, so breakfast is waiting in the fridge. Top with fruit, nuts or a spoon of peanut butter.
steps: Put the oats, chia seeds and cinnamon in a jar or container with a lid.
Pour in the milk, add the yogurt and honey and stir well, making sure no dry oats are stuck at the bottom.
Close the lid and leave it in the fridge overnight, or for at least 4 hours. The oats and chia soak up the liquid and turn soft and creamy.
In the morning give it a stir, loosen with a splash of milk if it's too thick, and top with berries and almonds. Eat it cold or warm it for a minute in the microwave.
keep: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot all the way through, covered so it doesn't dry out.

title: Homemade banana bread
summary: A moist, tender loaf with a golden crust, sweetened mostly by very ripe bananas. Even better the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth. The blacker the skins, the sweeter and more fragrant the bread will be.
Stir in the melted butter, then the sugar, egg and vanilla.
Sprinkle over the baking soda, salt and cinnamon, then fold in the flour (and the walnuts, if using) until no dry flour is left. Don't beat it: a gentle mix keeps the crumb soft.
Pour into the tin and bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. If the top browns too fast, cover it loosely with foil.
Let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift it out onto a rack. Wait until it's cool before slicing, so it doesn't crumble.
keep: Keep it covered or in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 days. Wrap cut edges so they don't dry out.

title: Classic chocolate brownies
summary: Fudgy, dense brownies with a shiny, crackly top. Take them out while the middle is still slightly soft.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 x 20 cm tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, or in short bursts in the microwave. Stir until smooth and let it cool for a few minutes.
In another bowl, whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla hard for 3 to 4 minutes until pale and thick. This is what gives brownies their shiny, crackly top.
Pour in the chocolate and fold it through, then sift over the flour, cocoa and salt and fold gently until just combined.
Spread into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes. The top should look set and cracked, but a skewer in the middle should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Leave to cool completely in the tin, ideally chilling for an hour, before cutting into 16 squares. They cut much more neatly once cold.
keep: Keep it covered or in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 days. Wrap cut edges so they don't dry out.

title: No-bake cheesecake
summary: A creamy, lightly lemony cheesecake on a buttery biscuit base, set in the fridge with no oven needed. Allow 6 hours to chill.
ingredients: 600 g full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
200 g berries or berry compote, to serve
steps: Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs in a food processor, or in a bag with a rolling pin. Mix them with the melted butter until they look like wet sand.
Press the crumbs firmly into the base of a 23 cm springform tin, using the bottom of a glass to pack them down. Chill while you make the filling.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar, vanilla, lemon zest and juice until smooth.
In another bowl, whip the cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the cream cheese until there are no streaks.
Spread the filling over the base, smooth the top and chill for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until firm.
Run a warm knife around the edge before opening the tin, and serve topped with berries.
keep: Keep it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Dairy-rich and set desserts shouldn't sit at room temperature for long.

title: Easy homemade chocolate mousse
summary: Airy, rich chocolate mousse made with just dark chocolate, eggs, a little sugar and cream. Needs 3 hours in the fridge.
steps: Melt the chocolate and butter together over a pan of barely simmering water, stir until smooth and leave to cool for 5 minutes, until just warm.
Stir the egg yolks into the chocolate one at a time.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it into the chocolate.
In a very clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then add the sugar a little at a time and keep whisking until you have soft, glossy peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the chocolate to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest with a big spoon, lifting from the bottom, until no white streaks remain. Go slowly so you keep the air in.
Spoon into glasses and chill for at least 3 hours, until set. Because the eggs are raw, use the freshest eggs you can find.
keep: Keep it covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Dairy-rich and set desserts shouldn't sit at room temperature for long.
